verdict.summary: Miro OAuth is self-serve: create an app in a free Developer team, share its installation URL, and any Miro user can authorize boards:read/boards:write the same day with no review, since Marketplace listing is optional (and now partner-gated). The friction is configuration and customer admins: the expiring-token choice is locked at app creation, and company admins can restrict members to approved apps only.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create a Developer team and app, set the redirect URI and scopes, install to your team, then wire the code exchange.

timeToProd.assumes: Private distribution via the app's installation URL with board read/write scopes; a public Marketplace listing is optional and adds partner approval plus a review of up to 8–12 weeks.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing — no review (customer company admins may need to approve the app if they restrict app installs)

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Miro states the Marketplace partner requirement doesn't affect privately distributed apps and that anyone with the installation link can install.

prerequisites.item: A Miro account and a Developer team
prerequisites.why: Apps are created and first installed in a Developer team; the OAuth guide lists it as a prerequisite.

prerequisites.item: A redirect URI registered in app settings
prerequisites.why: The redirect_uri must be configured on the app and match the value sent in the token exchange.

prerequisites.item: A decision on expiring vs non-expiring tokens before you create the app
prerequisites.why: The choice is made at creation time and can't be enabled, disabled or updated afterwards.

prerequisites.item: A public app/webhook URL if you use webhooks or a Web SDK panel
prerequisites.why: Miro webhooks can't be registered against a non-public URL, and LAN/VPN app URLs only work for people on that network.

scopeTiers.impact: Read and edit boards, members and items for whatever the user can access. This is what most agents need.
Projects scopes work on the REST API. identity and team scopes are listed for the Web SDK only, so they're of limited use to a headless REST agent.
Only work when the authorizing user is in an Enterprise organization (typically an admin). Not useful for a general consumer agent.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The scopes page lists these under 'Enterprise plan only'; who exactly can grant them is our inference.

scopeTiers.impact: Gated by the customer's add-on purchase, not by Miro reviewing your app.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The page labels them Enterprise Guard without explaining the gating.

steps.title: Create a Developer team
steps.detail: Sign in to Miro and create a free Developer team from the developer docs' getting-started flow.

steps.title: Decide token expiry and scopes
steps.detail: Pick expiring tokens (1 h access, 60-day rotating refresh) for production; the setting is permanent per app. List the minimal scopes, usually boards:read and boards:write.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: In Your apps, click Create new app, choose the Developer team, and tick the expiring-token option if wanted. Copy the client ID and secret.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Console URL resolved (302 to login); button names weren't observed because we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Configure redirect URI and permissions, then install
steps.detail: Add your redirect URI, tick the scopes, and click Install app and get OAuth token to test against your Developer team.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth code flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://miro.com/oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&state=.... Exchange the code with POST https://api.miro.com/v1/oauth/token (grant_type=authorization_code, client_id, client_secret, code, redirect_uri). Store team_id with the tokens.

steps.title: Implement refresh
steps.detail: POST grant_type=refresh_token to the same token endpoint. Each refresh returns a new refresh token and invalidates the old pair, so persist atomically.

steps.title: Handle rate limits
steps.detail: Budget against credit weights (Level 1 = 50 credits ... Level 4 = 2,000) and back off on 429 tooManyRequests using X-RateLimit-Reset.

steps.title: Share the installation URL
steps.detail: Copy the Installation URL from the bottom of the app's settings page under Share app and use it in your connect flow. Anyone with the link can install to a team they belong to.

steps.title: Optional: apply to list on the Marketplace
steps.detail: Fill in the Partner Interest Form. Only approved partners get the listing-submission link; Miro favours apps with customer demand and traction.

steps.title: Optional: Marketplace review
steps.detail: Partner approval (no stated timeline) followed by listing review; third-party summaries of Miro's docs cite up to 8–12 weeks.

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: The 8–12 week figure came from search summaries of Miro's 'Publish your app' page, which we didn't open.

agentCanDo: Choose minimal scopes and the token-expiry strategy
Implement the authorize, code exchange and rotating refresh flow
Build credit-aware rate limiting and 429 backoff
Draft admin-facing docs so customer admins can approve the app by client ID
Check the MCP server's OAuth metadata if using Miro MCP instead of REST
humanMustDo: Sign in to Miro and create the Developer team and app
Tick the expiring-token option at creation (it can't be changed later)
Install the app to the Developer team and copy client credentials
Fill in the Partner Interest Form if you want a Marketplace listing

blockers.symptom: Tokens never expire and there's no refresh_token, or you want to switch to expiring tokens later
blockers.cause: The app was created without the expiring-token option; it can't be enabled, disabled or updated after creation.
blockers.fix: Create a new app with expiring tokens and migrate users through re-authorization.

blockers.symptom: Refresh fails with an invalid token after a previous successful refresh
blockers.cause: Every refresh issues a new refresh token and invalidates the old pair; refresh tokens also lapse after 60 days unused.
blockers.fix: Persist the newest refresh token atomically and refresh before 60 days of inactivity.

blockers.symptom: Enterprise users can't add your app, or only see a request-access option
blockers.cause: Their company admin restricted members to an approved-apps list.
blockers.fix: Ask the admin to approve your app (internal apps can be approved by pasting the client ID).

evidence.label: unverified
evidence.note: From search summaries of Miro's help article 'App management', which returned 403 to our fetcher.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 with code tooManyRequests 'Request rate limit exceeded'
blockers.cause: The user-app pair exceeded its credit budget, or the app hit its global 100,000 credits/min.
blockers.fix: Back off using X-RateLimit-Reset and favour cheaper (Level 1) methods.

blockers.cause: Miro can't register webhooks with a non-public URL.
blockers.fix: Expose a public HTTPS endpoint (use a tunnel in development).

blockers.symptom: Your app doesn't appear in Miro's Marketplace even though it works
blockers.cause: Marketplace listing now needs partner approval first; private apps are only reachable via the installation URL.
blockers.fix: Distribute via the installation URL, or apply through the Partner Interest Form.

nuances.text: Expiring tokens: access tokens last 60 minutes and refresh tokens 60 days, rotating on each refresh. Non-expiring tokens last until the user uninstalls the app from the team.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The non-expiring lifetime wording came from search summaries; s6 confirms both modes exist.

nuances.text: Installs are per team: the token response carries a team_id, so a user in several teams may need to authorize once per team.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The OAuth guide shows team_id but doesn't explain team selection.

nuances.text: Rate limits are per user per app in credits (Level 1: 2,000 req/min ... Level 4: 50 req/min) with an app-wide ceiling of 100,000 credits per minute.

Miro also runs a hosted MCP server (mcp.miro.com) with its own OAuth 2.1 server, dynamic client registration and scopes boards:read, boards:write, openid, email; Miro says it works on all plans including free.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Fetched mcp.miro.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server on 2026-10-20: DCR endpoint, S256 PKCE, refresh_token and jwt-bearer grants.

nuances.text: identity:read and team:read are listed for the Web SDK only, so a REST-only agent may not be able to read the user's email via those scopes.
